items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And Eddie Halliday, a tough Irishman who would pull his coat off and fight... Eddie Halliday would come over there and cap the joint.

ctx.x: gangs on the riverfront, they're foremen... And Eddie Halliday, a tough Irishman who would pull his coat off and fight, and one got the gang...you know, test Eddie Halliday's Negroes, you know, insult them on the river, because Eddie Halliday would come over there and cap the joint.

They had a thing going. All the element of people, the poor oppressed Irishmen come here, starving from the potato famine, they settle in New Orleans. You have the Negro here. They're both working. They're rivals for the hardest work, uneducated work in town. But they have a common thing in one another. They were still longshoremen. So you don't say nothin' about these Nigger longshoremen and you don't say nothin' about them Irish longshoremen. They come over there and...
